_comment: Treasurer of the United States and Secretary of the Treasury, as they
appear on small-size US currency.
Signatures are the differentiator between Friedberg variants of the same
denomination and series year, so they are the field a lookup service most
needs. They are also safe to seed in a way a Friedberg table is not: who
held an office and when is historical fact, whereas the Friedberg
numbering is a copyrighted arrangement.
term_from and term_to bracket the years the pair signed together, so a
picker can offer only the combinations possible for a note's series year
instead of all of them. That is the intended use -- 'signature choices
based on series'.
THIS LIST IS PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY SO. Every pair here was confirmed
against published sources during a session on 2026-09-07: the 1935 series
run A-H, the 1957 run, 1963 and 1963A, and 1969. An attempt to extract a
complete chronology returned obviously corrupt rows -- six pairs with the
same surname in both columns -- and was discarded rather than seeded.
The gaps are the point of the seed-and-extend model: add what is missing
from the note in hand, and it is marked `manual` so a later reload never
overwrites it. Anything added by hand should be checked against the note
itself before it is trusted for a catalogue lookup.
Naming: `code` is treasurer_secretary in lower case, which is how dealers
write it (Julian/Morgenthau). `label` is the same pair as displayed.
